input.quote: 26. APPLICABLE LAW. This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).
input.rationale: Section 26 selects California law and Section 27 sends all disputes "solely and exclusively" to the state or federal courts located in San Luis Obispo County, California, with consent to jurisdiction and a waiver of venue/forum objections. California is an accepted governing law and the forum is the corresponding California courts, so the clause sits at the fallback position on its material terms. There is no arbitration provision anywhere in the Agreement (no arbitration clause surfaced on search), so the walk-away risk of mandatory foreign-seated arbitration is not present. It falls short of the preferred position only in that it is not New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County, and the venue clause does not carve out temporary injunctive relief elsewhere; those are preferred-only refinements noted here rather than redlined. We also note Section 18 imports the California Uniform Commercial Code and Section 23 references California Civil Code section 1654, which are consistent with the retained California choice of law.
